Ratio of areas of two triangles is equal to the ratio of the products of their bases and corresponding heights.

\(\frac{A(\text{first triangle})}{A(\text{second triangle})} = \frac{9 \times 5}{10 \times 6} = \frac{45}{60} = \frac{3}{4}\)

\(\therefore\) the ratio of the areas is \(\frac{3}{4}\), i.e. 3 : 4.

seg BC \(\perp\) seg AB and seg AD \(\perp\) seg AB, so AB is a common base of \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle ADB\), and BC and AD are their corresponding heights.

Areas of triangles with equal bases are proportional to their corresponding heights.

\(\therefore \frac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle ADB)} = \frac{BC}{AD} = \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}\)

\(\triangle PQR\) has two pairs of base and corresponding height: base RQ with height PS, and base PR with height QT. Both give the same area.

\(\frac{1}{2} \times RQ \times PS = \frac{1}{2} \times PR \times QT\)

\(\therefore RQ \times PS = PR \times QT\)

\(\therefore 6 \times 6 = 12 \times QT\)

\(\therefore QT = \frac{36}{12} = 3\)

\(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle BCD\) have the common base BC.

AD \(\parallel\) BC, and the vertices A and D both lie on line AD. The distance between the two parallel lines is therefore the height of both triangles, so their heights are equal.

Areas of triangles with equal bases are proportional to their corresponding heights.

\(\therefore \frac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle BCD)} = \frac{1}{1}\)

\(\therefore A(\triangle ABC) : A(\triangle BCD) = 1 : 1\)

(i) \(\triangle PQB\) and \(\triangle PBC\) have the common vertex P and their bases QB and BC lie on the same line BC, so their heights are equal.

\(\therefore \frac{A(\triangle PQB)}{A(\triangle PBC)} = \frac{BQ}{BC}\) .......... areas proportional to bases

(ii) \(\triangle PBC\) and \(\triangle ABC\) have the common base BC, with heights PQ and AD.

\(\therefore \frac{A(\triangle PBC)}{A(\triangle ABC)} = \frac{PQ}{AD}\) .......... areas proportional to heights

(iii) \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle ADC\) have the common vertex A and their bases BC and DC lie on the same line, so their heights are equal.

\(\therefore \frac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle ADC)} = \frac{BC}{DC}\)

(iv) \(\triangle ADC\) has base DC and height AD; \(\triangle PQC\) has base QC and height PQ. Here neither the bases nor the heights are equal, so the general result is used.

\(\therefore \frac{A(\triangle ADC)}{A(\triangle PQC)} = \frac{DC \times AD}{QC \times PQ}\)

By the converse of the theorem of the bisector of an angle of a triangle, ray PM bisects \(\angle QPR\) exactly when \(\frac{PQ}{PR} = \frac{QM}{MR}\).

(1) \(\frac{PQ}{PR} = \frac{7}{3}\) and \(\frac{QM}{MR} = \frac{3.5}{1.5} = \frac{7}{3}\). They are equal, so ray PM **is** the bisector of \(\angle QPR\).

(2) \(\frac{PR}{PQ} = \frac{7}{10}\) and \(\frac{RM}{MQ} = \frac{6}{8} = \frac{3}{4}\). They are not equal, so ray PM **is not** the bisector of \(\angle QPR\).

(3) \(\frac{PQ}{PR} = \frac{9}{10}\) and \(\frac{QM}{MR} = \frac{3.6}{4} = \frac{9}{10}\). They are equal, so ray PM **is** the bisector of \(\angle QPR\).

M lies on side PQ and N lies on side PR.

PQ = 25 and PM = 15 \(\therefore\) MQ = 25 \(-\) 15 = 10

PR = 20 and NR = 8 \(\therefore\) PN = 20 \(-\) 8 = 12

\(\frac{PM}{MQ} = \frac{15}{10} = \frac{3}{2}\) and \(\frac{PN}{NR} = \frac{12}{8} = \frac{3}{2}\)

\(\therefore \frac{PN}{NR} = \frac{PM}{MQ} = \frac{3}{2}\)

The line NM divides the two sides PR and PQ of \(\triangle PQR\) in the same ratio.

\(\therefore\) line NM \(\parallel\) side RQ .......... converse of basic proportionality theorem

In \(\triangle MNP\), seg NQ bisects \(\angle N\) and Q lies on side MP.

\(\frac{MN}{PN} = \frac{MQ}{QP}\) .......... property of an angle bisector of a triangle

\(\frac{5}{7} = \frac{2.5}{QP}\)

\(\therefore QP = \frac{2.5 \times 7}{5} = 3.5\)

\(\angle APQ = 60^\circ\) and \(\angle ABC = 60^\circ\) .......... given

\(\therefore \angle APQ \cong \angle ABC\)

These are corresponding angles formed by line PQ and line BC with the transversal AB.

\(\therefore\) seg PQ \(\parallel\) seg BC .......... corresponding angles test

In \(\triangle ABC\), the line PQ is parallel to side BC and intersects the remaining sides AB and AC in the distinct points P and Q.

\(\therefore \frac{AP}{PB} = \frac{AQ}{QC}\) .......... basic proportionality theorem

In trapezium ABCD, side AB \(\parallel\) side PQ \(\parallel\) side DC, with P on side AD and Q on side BC. AD and BC are the two transversals of these three parallel lines.

The ratio of the intercepts made on one transversal by three parallel lines is equal to the ratio of the corresponding intercepts on any other transversal.

\(\therefore \frac{AP}{PD} = \frac{BQ}{QC}\)

\(\therefore \frac{15}{12} = \frac{BQ}{14}\)

\(\therefore BQ = \frac{15 \times 14}{12} = \frac{210}{12} = 17.5\)

In \(\triangle MNP\), seg NQ bisects \(\angle N\) and Q lies on side MP. From the figure MN = 25, MQ = 14 and NP = 40.

\(\frac{MN}{NP} = \frac{MQ}{QP}\) .......... property of an angle bisector of a triangle

\(\frac{25}{40} = \frac{14}{QP}\)

\(\therefore QP = \frac{14 \times 40}{25} = \frac{560}{25} = 22.4\)

AB \(\parallel\) CD \(\parallel\) FE are three parallel lines cut by two transversals. B, D, F are the intercept points on one transversal and A, C, E on the other.

\(\frac{BD}{DF} = \frac{AC}{CE}\) .......... property of three parallel lines and their transversals

\(\frac{8}{4} = \frac{12}{x}\)

\(\therefore 8x = 48\) \(\therefore x = 6\)

A \(-\) C \(-\) E, so AE = AC + CE = 12 + 6 = 18

\(\therefore x = 6\) and AE = 18

In \(\triangle LMN\), ray MT bisects \(\angle LMN\) and T lies on side LN.

\(\frac{LM}{MN} = \frac{LT}{TN}\) .......... property of an angle bisector of a triangle

\(\frac{6}{10} = \frac{LT}{8}\)

\(\therefore LT = \frac{6 \times 8}{10} = 4.8\)

In \(\triangle ABC\), seg BD bisects \(\angle ABC\) and D lies on side AC.

\(\frac{AB}{BC} = \frac{AD}{DC}\) .......... property of an angle bisector of a triangle

\(\frac{x}{x + 5} = \frac{x - 2}{x + 2}\)

\(\therefore x(x + 2) = (x - 2)(x + 5)\)

\(\therefore x^2 + 2x = x^2 + 3x - 10\)

\(\therefore 2x = 3x - 10\)

\(\therefore x = 10\)

[Textbook misprint: the last line of the printed proof reads 'seg PR \(\parallel\) seg DE'. That is a misprint — the question itself asks for seg PR \(\parallel\) seg DF, and DF is what follows from \(\frac{XP}{PD} = \frac{XR}{RF}\). The printed ANSWERS section does not cover this line.]

In \(\triangle XDE\), PQ \(\parallel\) DE .......... **given**

\(\therefore \frac{XP}{PD} = \frac{XQ}{QE}\) .......... (I) (Basic proportionality theorem)

In \(\triangle XEF\), QR \(\parallel\) EF .......... **given**

\(\therefore \frac{XR}{RF} = \frac{XQ}{QE}\) .......... (II) **(Basic proportionality theorem)**

\(\therefore \frac{XP}{PD} = \frac{XR}{RF}\) .......... from (I) and (II)

In \(\triangle XDF\), the point P lies on side XD and R lies on side XF, and these two sides are divided in the same ratio.

\(\therefore\) seg PR \(\parallel\) seg DF .......... (converse of basic proportionality theorem)

In \(\triangle ABC\), ray BD bisects \(\angle ABC\) and D lies on side AC.

\(\therefore \frac{AB}{BC} = \frac{AD}{DC}\) .......... (I) property of an angle bisector of a triangle

In \(\triangle ABC\), ray CE bisects \(\angle ACB\) and E lies on side AB.

\(\therefore \frac{AC}{BC} = \frac{AE}{EB}\) .......... (II) property of an angle bisector of a triangle

seg AB \(\cong\) seg AC \(\therefore\) AB = AC .......... (III) given

From (I), (II) and (III), \(\frac{AD}{DC} = \frac{AB}{BC} = \frac{AC}{BC} = \frac{AE}{EB}\)

\(\therefore \frac{AE}{EB} = \frac{AD}{DC}\)

In \(\triangle ABC\), E lies on side AB and D lies on side AC, and these two sides are divided in the same ratio.

\(\therefore\) seg ED \(\parallel\) seg BC .......... converse of basic proportionality theorem

In \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle EDC\),

\(\angle ABC \cong \angle EDC\) .......... each is \(75^\circ\), given

\(\angle ACB \cong \angle ECD\) .......... common angle

\(\therefore \triangle ABC \sim \triangle EDC\) .......... AA test of similarity

In \(\triangle PQR\) and \(\triangle LMN\),

\(\frac{PQ}{LM} = \frac{6}{3} = \frac{2}{1}\)

\(\frac{QR}{MN} = \frac{8}{4} = \frac{2}{1}\)

\(\frac{PR}{LN} = \frac{10}{5} = \frac{2}{1}\)

\(\therefore \frac{PQ}{LM} = \frac{QR}{MN} = \frac{PR}{LN}\)

Three sides of one triangle are in proportion to the corresponding three sides of the other.

\(\therefore \triangle PQR \sim \triangle LMN\) .......... SSS test of similarity

Both poles are perpendicular to the ground and the sunlight falls at the same angle at the same time, so the two pole-and-shadow triangles have two pairs of congruent angles and are similar by the AA test.

\(\therefore \frac{\text{height of smaller pole}}{\text{height of bigger pole}} = \frac{\text{shadow of smaller pole}}{\text{shadow of bigger pole}}\)

Let the shadow of the bigger pole be \(x\) m.

\(\frac{4}{8} = \frac{6}{x}\)

\(\therefore 4x = 48\) \(\therefore x = 12\)

\(\therefore\) the shadow of the bigger pole is 12 metre long.

In \(\triangle CPA\) and \(\triangle CQB\),

\(\angle CPA \cong \angle CQB\) .......... each is \(90^\circ\), since AP \(\perp\) BC and BQ \(\perp\) AC

\(\angle ACP \cong \angle BCQ\) .......... common angle (B \(-\) P \(-\) C and A \(-\) Q \(-\) C)

\(\therefore \triangle CPA \sim \triangle CQB\) .......... AA test of similarity

\(\therefore \frac{PA}{QB} = \frac{CA}{CB}\) .......... corresponding sides of similar triangles

\(\therefore \frac{7}{8} = \frac{AC}{12}\)

\(\therefore AC = \frac{7 \times 12}{8} = 10.5\)

In trapezium PQRS, side PQ \(\parallel\) side SR and the diagonals PR and QS intersect at A.

In \(\triangle APQ\) and \(\triangle ARS\),

\(\angle PAQ \cong \angle RAS\) .......... opposite angles

\(\angle APQ \cong \angle ARS\) .......... alternate angles, since PQ \(\parallel\) SR and PR is a transversal

\(\therefore \triangle APQ \sim \triangle ARS\) .......... AA test of similarity

\(\therefore \frac{AP}{AR} = \frac{PQ}{RS}\) .......... corresponding sides of similar triangles

AR = 5AP \(\therefore \frac{AP}{AR} = \frac{1}{5}\)

\(\therefore \frac{PQ}{RS} = \frac{1}{5}\)

\(\therefore\) SR = 5PQ

In trapezium ABCD, side AB \(\parallel\) side DC and the diagonals AC and BD intersect at O.

In \(\triangle AOB\) and \(\triangle COD\),

\(\angle OAB \cong \angle OCD\) .......... alternate angles, since AB \(\parallel\) DC and AC is a transversal

\(\angle AOB \cong \angle COD\) .......... opposite angles

\(\therefore \triangle AOB \sim \triangle COD\) .......... AA test of similarity

\(\therefore \frac{AB}{CD} = \frac{OB}{OD}\) .......... corresponding sides of similar triangles

\(\therefore \frac{20}{6} = \frac{15}{OD}\)

\(\therefore OD = \frac{15 \times 6}{20} = 4.5\)

\(\square\) ABCD is a parallelogram, so side AB \(\parallel\) side DC.

In \(\triangle BET\) and \(\triangle CED\),

\(\angle BET \cong \angle CED\) .......... opposite angles

\(\angle EBT \cong \angle ECD\) .......... alternate angles, since AB \(\parallel\) DC and BC is a transversal

\(\therefore \triangle BET \sim \triangle CED\) .......... AA test of similarity

\(\therefore \frac{BE}{CE} = \frac{TE}{DE}\) .......... corresponding sides of similar triangles

\(\therefore DE \times BE = CE \times TE\)

In \(\triangle ABP\) and \(\triangle CDP\),

\(\frac{AP}{CP} = \frac{BP}{DP}\) .......... given

\(\angle APB \cong \angle CPD\) .......... opposite angles

Two pairs of corresponding sides are in the same proportion and the angles included by them are congruent.

\(\therefore \triangle ABP \sim \triangle CDP\) .......... SAS test of similarity

In \(\triangle ACB\) and \(\triangle DCA\),

\(\angle BAC \cong \angle ADC\) .......... given

\(\angle ACB \cong \angle DCA\) .......... common angle (B \(-\) D \(-\) C)

\(\therefore \triangle ACB \sim \triangle DCA\) .......... AA test of similarity

\(\therefore \frac{CA}{CD} = \frac{CB}{CA}\) .......... corresponding sides of similar triangles

\(\therefore CA^2 = CB \times CD\)

When two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides.

Ratio of corresponding sides = 3 : 5

\(\therefore\) ratio of areas \(= \frac{3^2}{5^2} = \frac{9}{25}\)

\(\therefore\) the ratio of their areas is 9 : 25.

\(\frac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle PQR)} = \frac{AB^2}{PQ^2} = \frac{2^2}{3^2} = \frac{4}{9}\)

The blanks are \(PQ^2\), then 4 and 9.

\(\frac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle PQR)} = \frac{80}{125} = \frac{16}{25}\)

When two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas equals the ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides.

\(\therefore \frac{AB^2}{PQ^2} = \frac{16}{25}\)

\(\therefore \frac{AB}{PQ} = \frac{4}{5}\) .......... taking square roots

The blanks are \(A(\triangle PQR)\), then 4 and 5.

\(9 \times A(\triangle PQR) = 16 \times A(\triangle LMN)\)

\(\therefore \frac{A(\triangle LMN)}{A(\triangle PQR)} = \frac{9}{16}\)

\(\triangle LMN \sim \triangle PQR\), and MN and QR are corresponding sides.

\(\therefore \frac{A(\triangle LMN)}{A(\triangle PQR)} = \frac{MN^2}{QR^2}\) .......... theorem of areas of similar triangles

\(\therefore \frac{MN^2}{QR^2} = \frac{9}{16}\) \(\therefore \frac{MN}{QR} = \frac{3}{4}\) .......... taking square roots

\(\therefore \frac{MN}{20} = \frac{3}{4}\) \(\therefore MN = 15\)

The two triangles are similar, so the ratio of their areas equals the ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides.

\(\frac{\text{area of bigger}}{\text{area of smaller}} = \frac{225}{81}\)

\(\therefore \frac{(\text{side of bigger})^2}{(\text{side of smaller})^2} = \frac{225}{81}\)

\(\therefore \frac{\text{side of bigger}}{\text{side of smaller}} = \frac{15}{9} = \frac{5}{3}\) .......... taking square roots

\(\therefore \frac{\text{side of bigger}}{12} = \frac{5}{3}\)

\(\therefore\) side of the bigger triangle \(= \frac{12 \times 5}{3} = 20\) cm

All equilateral triangles are similar to one another, because each of their angles measures \(60^\circ\).

\(\therefore \frac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle DEF)} = \frac{AB^2}{DE^2}\) .......... theorem of areas of similar triangles

\(\therefore \frac{1}{2} = \frac{4^2}{DE^2}\)

\(\therefore DE^2 = 2 \times 16 = 32\)

\(\therefore DE = \sqrt{32} = 4\sqrt{2}\)

\(A(\triangle PQF) = 20\) units, PF = 2 DP, Let us assume DP = \(x\). \(\therefore\) PF = \(2x\)

DF = DP + **PF** = \(x\) + \(2x\) = \(3x\)

In \(\triangle FDE\) and \(\triangle FPQ\),

\(\angle FDE \cong \angle\) **FPQ** .......... corresponding angles

\(\angle FED \cong \angle\) **FQP** .......... corresponding angles

\(\therefore \triangle FDE \sim \triangle FPQ\) .......... AA test

\(\therefore \frac{A(\triangle FDE)}{A(\triangle FPQ)} = \frac{DF^2}{PF^2} = \frac{(3x)^2}{(2x)^2} = \frac{9}{4}\)

\(A(\triangle FDE) = \frac{9}{4} A(\triangle FPQ) = \frac{9}{4} \times 20 = 45\)

\(A(\square DPQE) = A(\triangle FDE) - A(\triangle FPQ)\)

\(= 45 - 20\)

\(= 25\) sq. unit

B \(-\) D \(-\) C, BD = 7 and BC = 20 \(\therefore\) DC = BC \(-\) BD = 20 \(-\) 7 = 13

A is the common vertex of \(\triangle ABD\), \(\triangle ADC\) and \(\triangle ABC\), and their bases BD, DC and BC lie on the same line, so all three heights are equal. Areas are therefore proportional to the bases.

(1) \(\frac{A(\triangle ABD)}{A(\triangle ADC)} = \frac{BD}{DC} = \frac{7}{13}\)

(2) \(\frac{A(\triangle ABD)}{A(\triangle ABC)} = \frac{BD}{BC} = \frac{7}{20}\)

(3) \(\frac{A(\triangle ADC)}{A(\triangle ABC)} = \frac{DC}{BC} = \frac{13}{20}\)

Areas of triangles with equal heights are proportional to their corresponding bases.

Let the base of the bigger triangle be \(x\) cm.

\(\frac{2}{3} = \frac{6}{x}\)

\(\therefore 2x = 18\) \(\therefore x = 9\)

\(\therefore\) the corresponding base of the bigger triangle is 9 cm.

\(\angle ABC = \angle DCB = 90^\circ\), so seg AB \(\perp\) seg BC and seg DC \(\perp\) seg BC.

\(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DCB\) have the common base BC, with heights AB and DC.

Areas of triangles with equal bases are proportional to their corresponding heights.

\(\therefore \frac{A(\triangle ABC)}{A(\triangle DCB)} = \frac{AB}{DC} = \frac{6}{8} = \frac{3}{4}\)

seg PM \(\perp\) seg QS, so PM is the height of \(\triangle PQS\) on the base QS.

\(A(\triangle PQS) = \frac{1}{2} \times QS \times PM\)

\(100 = \frac{1}{2} \times QS \times 10\)

\(\therefore QS = 20\) cm

seg NR \(\perp\) seg QS, so NR is the height of \(\triangle QRS\) on the same base QS.

\(A(\triangle QRS) = \frac{1}{2} \times QS \times NR\)

\(110 = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times NR\)

\(\therefore NR = 11\) cm

\(\triangle MNT \sim \triangle QRS\), and the altitudes drawn from T and from S are corresponding altitudes. Let them be TD and SE, on the corresponding bases MN and QR.

In the chapter's proof of the theorem of areas of similar triangles it is shown that the two triangles formed by a pair of corresponding altitudes are similar by the AA test, so a pair of corresponding altitudes is in the same ratio as a pair of corresponding sides.

\(\therefore \frac{TD}{SE} = \frac{MN}{QR} = \frac{5}{9}\)

\(\therefore \frac{A(\triangle MNT)}{A(\triangle QRS)} = \frac{MN^2}{QR^2}\) .......... theorem of areas of similar triangles

\(\therefore \frac{A(\triangle MNT)}{A(\triangle QRS)} = \frac{5^2}{9^2} = \frac{25}{81}\)

The same value follows directly from the areas: \(\frac{A(\triangle MNT)}{A(\triangle QRS)} = \frac{MN \times TD}{QR \times SE} = \frac{5}{9} \times \frac{5}{9} = \frac{25}{81}\)

In \(\triangle ABC\), A \(-\) D \(-\) C and B \(-\) E \(-\) C, and seg DE \(\parallel\) side AB.

\(\therefore \frac{CD}{DA} = \frac{CE}{EB}\) .......... basic proportionality theorem

Let BE = \(x\). B \(-\) E \(-\) C and BC = 6.4 \(\therefore\) CE = 6.4 \(-\) \(x\)

\(\therefore \frac{3}{5} = \frac{6.4 - x}{x}\)

\(\therefore 3x = 5(6.4 - x) = 32 - 5x\)

\(\therefore 8x = 32\) \(\therefore x = 4\)

\(\therefore\) BE = 4

seg PA, seg QB, seg RC and seg SD are all perpendicular to line AD, so they are parallel to one another. Line AD and line PS are two transversals of these parallel lines.

The intercepts made on one transversal are proportional to the corresponding intercepts on the other.

\(\therefore \frac{PQ}{AB} = \frac{QR}{BC} = \frac{RS}{CD} = \frac{PQ + QR + RS}{AB + BC + CD} = \frac{PS}{AD}\)

AD = AB + BC + CD = 60 + 70 + 80 = 210 and PS = 280

\(\therefore \frac{PS}{AD} = \frac{280}{210} = \frac{4}{3}\)

\(\therefore PQ = 60 \times \frac{4}{3} = 80\)

\(\therefore QR = 70 \times \frac{4}{3} = \frac{280}{3}\)

\(\therefore RS = 80 \times \frac{4}{3} = \frac{320}{3}\)

Check: \(80 + \frac{280}{3} + \frac{320}{3} = \frac{240 + 280 + 320}{3} = \frac{840}{3} = 280 = PS\)

In \(\triangle PMQ\), ray MX is bisector of \(\angle PMQ\).

\(\therefore \frac{MP}{MQ} = \frac{PX}{XQ}\) .......... (I) theorem of angle bisector.

In \(\triangle PMR\), ray MY is bisector of \(\angle PMR\).

\(\therefore \frac{MP}{MR} = \frac{PY}{YR}\) .......... (II) theorem of angle bisector.

But \(\frac{MP}{MQ} = \frac{MP}{MR}\) .......... M is the midpoint of QR, hence MQ = MR.

\(\therefore \frac{PX}{XQ} = \frac{PY}{YR}\)

In \(\triangle PQR\), X lies on side PQ and Y on side PR, and these two sides are divided in the same ratio.

\(\therefore\) XY \(\parallel\) QR .......... converse of basic proportionality theorem.

X is the point of intersection of the bisectors of \(\angle B\) and \(\angle C\), so ray AX is the bisector of \(\angle A\) and it meets side BC at Y.

In \(\triangle ABC\), ray AY bisects \(\angle BAC\).

\(\therefore \frac{BY}{YC} = \frac{AB}{AC} = \frac{5}{4}\) .......... property of an angle bisector of a triangle

B \(-\) Y \(-\) C and BC = 6

\(\therefore BY = 6 \times \frac{5}{9} = \frac{10}{3}\)

In \(\triangle ABY\), ray BX bisects \(\angle ABY\) and X lies on side AY.

\(\therefore \frac{AX}{XY} = \frac{AB}{BY}\) .......... property of an angle bisector of a triangle

\(\therefore \frac{AX}{XY} = \frac{5}{\frac{10}{3}} = \frac{15}{10} = \frac{3}{2}\)

seg AD \(\parallel\) seg BC and the diagonals AC and BD intersect at P.

In \(\triangle APD\) and \(\triangle CPB\),

\(\angle PAD \cong \angle PCB\) .......... alternate angles, since AD \(\parallel\) BC and AC is a transversal

\(\angle APD \cong \angle CPB\) .......... opposite angles

\(\therefore \triangle APD \sim \triangle CPB\) .......... AA test of similarity

\(\therefore \frac{AP}{CP} = \frac{PD}{PB}\) .......... corresponding sides of similar triangles

\(\therefore AP \times PB = CP \times PD\)

\(\therefore \frac{AP}{PD} = \frac{PC}{BP}\)

2AX = 3BX \(\therefore \frac{AX}{BX} = \frac{3}{2}\)

\(\frac{AX + BX}{BX} = \frac{3 + 2}{2}\) .......... by componendo.

\(\frac{AB}{BX} = \frac{5}{2}\) .......... (I)

\(\triangle BCA \sim \triangle BYX\) .......... **AA** test of similarity

\(\therefore \frac{BA}{BX} = \frac{AC}{XY}\) .......... corresponding sides of similar triangles.

\(\therefore \frac{5}{2} = \frac{AC}{9}\) \(\therefore AC = \frac{5 \times 9}{2} = 22.5\) ...from (I)

Check: BX = 2 and AX = 3 satisfy 2AX = 3BX, so AB = 5 and \(\frac{XY}{AC} = \frac{BX}{BA} = \frac{2}{5}\), giving \(AC = 9 \times \frac{5}{2} = 22.5\).

DEFG is a square, so GD = DE = EF and seg GD \(\perp\) seg BC, seg FE \(\perp\) seg BC.

In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle A = 90^\circ\)

\(\therefore \angle B + \angle C = 90^\circ\) .......... sum of the angles of a triangle

In \(\triangle GBD\), \(\angle GDB = 90^\circ\)

\(\therefore \angle BGD = 90^\circ - \angle B = \angle C\)

In \(\triangle GBD\) and \(\triangle CFE\),

\(\angle GDB \cong \angle CEF\) .......... each is \(90^\circ\)

\(\angle BGD \cong \angle FCE\) .......... proved above, each equals \(\angle C\)

\(\therefore \triangle GBD \sim \triangle CFE\) .......... AA test of similarity

\(\therefore \frac{GD}{CE} = \frac{BD}{FE}\) .......... corresponding sides of similar triangles

\(\therefore GD \times FE = BD \times CE\)

But GD = FE = DE .......... sides of the square DEFG

\(\therefore DE \times DE = BD \times EC\)

\(\therefore DE^2 = BD \times EC\)
